transcription: Verdicts and corrected fields copied verbatim from the verificador's final message; reasons condensed by the build session.

verdicts.reason: Verbatim on page 16; states the experiment ran under long-term microgravity. Its priority claim ('the first experiment') must never be repeated by PYRION.
Verbatim on page 24; every PSI row is a 2009 flight session; no ground rows.
Second-hand 1-g results (Dotson thesis); test_id names no PSI test, so not ingested; the report contradicts itself on the comparison.
Verbatim on page 12, 'fuel gases'; psia values are bottle fill pressures, not test pressure.
Lineage incomplete: BASS and BASS-II used the SPICE apparatus.

corrected.derivation: Facility on the ISS. The SPICE apparatus installed in the MSG is a modified version of the apparatus built for Enclosed Laminar Flames (ELF) (Final Report page 9). Not stated in the three sources read, but documented elsewhere in PSI: BASS burned its samples in the SPICE flow duct (psi-data/PSI-26/Science Documents/PSI-26_Science Documents_FlammabilityAspectsofFabric_USNationalCombustion.2013.docx, paragraph=51: 'The samples are burned in the SPICE apparatus which is a small flow duct with a cross-sectional area of 76mm x 76mm [Dotson et. al. 2010].'), and BASS-II procedures run in the 'SPICE Experiment Assembly' (psi-data/PSI-25/Engineering Documents/PSI-25_Engineering Documents_BASS-II_Ops.docx, paragraph=60). The project lineage list says SLICE shares the same duct; PSI-106 files do not confirm it. PSI-60 (ground investigation) re-analyses SPICE data sets. SPICE, BASS and BASS-II results come from the same flow duct and must not be counted as independent apparatus.

verdicts.reason: The sentence's 5.4-65 cm/s is the smoke-point range; the PSI table has rows below it.

corrected.derivation: Burner diameters and co-flow velocities are in the PSI table and are not extracted here. The 5.4-65 cm/s range in this sentence is the smoke-point range of Final Report Table 1 (page 20); the PSI table has rows below it: 4.42 cm/s (data rows 248-249) and -0.28 / 0.66 cm/s (data rows 295-300, GMT day 136, 75 % Propylene, 0.4064 mm nozzle). The per-test Air Rate in the table governs those tests.

verdicts.reason: 'no SPICE test is quiescent' is contradicted by near-zero table rows.

corrected.derivation: The apparatus keeps a minimum fan voltage even at fan dial setting 0 (page 16). This does not show that every test had a measurable coflow: the PSI table records Air Rate -0.28 and 0.66 cm/s for data rows 295-300 (GMT day 136), while the ground calibration in Fig. 14 (page 17, read from the plot) shows roughly 9-15 cm/s at dial 0; the sources do not explain the difference. The per-test Air Rate in the table governs those tests.

verdicts.reason: 19-24% is the ISS cabin specification band, not a test O2.
Calculation assumption (21±1% O2): ambiguous, never counted.
Calculation assumption (101 kPa): ambiguous, never counted.
Co-flow is ISS cabin air: N2 derived; fuel-mixture N2 kept apart.

missed: flame_type: page 21 (fuel jet into air) implies 'normal'; not proposed by the extractor; not ingested.
298 K in the Table 1 footnote is a calculation assumption, not a measurement.
Lineage: BASS and BASS-II used the SPICE duct; PSI-60 re-analyses SPICE data.
could_not_check: Dotson thesis and other PSI-107 files not opened (pressure confirmed absent only in the three listed sources); cause of near-zero Air Rate rows unresolved; SLICE sharing the duct not confirmed from PSI; duct size differs between sources.
review_level: segregated internal check by a language model; not expert or NASA review
